name: Planetarium latitude study
summary: Nainoa Thompson and Will Kyselka used a planetarium sky set to different latitudes to learn which star positions could tell a navigator how far north or south he was.
description: Thompson and Kyselka varied simulated latitude to study star rise/set positions and candidate latitude cues.
tier_reason: A particular planetarium preparation method is fine detail, with its own role before the voyage. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.
why: Preparing to navigate Hōkūleʻa himself, Thompson needed latitude cues, and the planetarium could show the sky as seen from any latitude.
